bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for case:ca3125c6ca6002055d70, the selected result — an exact two-sided binomial test declaring a statistically significant bias away from the UV-marked arm (5 of 20 bouts, p = 0.041389) — is not supported, because the 20 rows entered as independent Bernoulli trials are repeated bouts from only 6 independent units (bee_id), each contributing 2–4 rows. The binomial test assumes row independence; the report's own per-bee tallies show strong within-bee consistency (three bees chose 'plain' in all 11 of their combined bouts, one bee chose 'uv_marked' in both of its bouts), and at the bee level only 1 of 6 bees showed a majority UV-marked preference, so the significance claim depends on the pseudoreplicated n = 20 rather than the 6 independent units.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding in three ways. (1) Computation check: I recomputed the exact two-sided binomial p-value for 5 successes in 20 trials against 0.5 — P(X<=5)+P(X>=15) = 2*21700/1048576 = 0.041389 — which matches the report, ruling out the alternative explanation that the significance claim is a mere arithmetic error rather than a unit-of-analysis error. (2) Independence check: I asked whether the 20 rows could plausibly behave as independent trials despite sharing bee IDs; the per-bee tallies refute this, since bees B01–B03 chose 'plain' in all 11 of their bouts and B04 chose 'uv_marked' in both of its bouts, a pattern showing strong within-bee correlation of outcomes. (3) Robustness check: I asked whether the conclusion would survive analysis at the designated independent unit; with 6 bees, only 1 has a majority UV-marked share (B04), 3 have zero, and a sign test or exact binomial on 6 units with any reasonable dichotomization cannot reach p < 0.05 (minimum attainable two-sided p with n=6 is 2/64 ≈ 0.031, requiring a 6-0 or 0-6 split, which does not occur). All three attempts failed to overturn the finding, so the significant conclusion is attributable to repeated entry of the 6 authorized independent units (bee_id) into the row-independent binomial procedure.

root_cause: The workflow counts every row of data/input.csv as one Bernoulli trial (n_bouts = len(bouts); n_marked summed over rows) and passes these row-level counts directly to scipy.stats.binomtest(n_marked, n_bouts, 0.5), a procedure whose sampling model requires each of the n trials to be an independent draw. Because the data description designates bee_id as the independent-unit column and each of the 6 bees is authorized to appear in 2–4 rows by the repeated-release design, the same independent unit repeatedly enters the row-independent procedure, inflating the effective sample size from 6 units to 20 rows and producing an unwarranted p < 0.05.
